content.title: MGM Resorts (MGM) Stock Trades Up, Here Is Why
content.summary: Shares of hospitality and casino entertainment company MGM Resorts (NYSE:MGM) jumped 3.8% in the afternoon session after its BetMGM joint venture reported strong third-quarter results and raised its full-year guidance.

content.title: The Market Selloff That Wasn’t
content.summary: The three major stock market indexes were all in the red as of late Tuesday morning.  The S&P 500, a market-cap weighted index, was down about 0.5%, dragged lower by losses in megacap techs (and artificial intelligence darlings) such as Nvidia, Oracle, Broadcom and Arista Networks.  Wells Fargo was a top gainer in the index following solid earnings. Ditto for Domino’s Pizza, a recent Barron’s stock pick. Casino stocks MGM Resorts, Las Vegas Sands and Wynn Resorts were rallying too, as were Airbnb and retailers Walmart and Dollar Tree.

content.title: BetMGM Lifts Full-Year Guidance After Strong Growth in IGaming, Online Sports
content.summary: BetMGM lifted its full-year earnings guidance after it reported a strong third-quarter performance boosted by growth in its iGaming and online sports divisions.  The sports-betting company—co-owned by  MGM Resorts International  and Entain—now expects net revenue of at least $2.75 billion and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization of around $200 million.  BetMGM said its so-called contribution from operations—a metric that deducts cost of revenue and marketing-acquisition spending from net revenue—is still expected to exceed $500 million.
